tasks.short: Attend training to maintain current fire prevention and firefighting knowledge.

steps.what: Attend training classes and practise current fire prevention, safety, and firefighting procedures

tasks.design: Keep attendance, practice, and questions with the fire inspector. Existing {LMS} material supports the course without replacing participation or demonstrated understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning requires the inspector to absorb and practise procedures.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital course access is already possible but does not establish a reduction in required learning time.
tasks.still_hard: Applying procedures to unfamiliar fire conditions requires judgement and practice.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector recognises gaps in understanding and asks scenario specific questions.
tasks.altitude: Maintain practical competence through active learning.

reach.learn: Where written procedures meet difficult field conditions

evidence.claim: Course attendance and practical learning cannot be credited as removed work merely because training material is digital.

assumptions: The task boundary is attending training, not creating materials or administering course records.
Existing LMS access receives no new saving credit; native delivery remains sufficient.
No machine step or structured competence flag is proposed; understanding remains assessed through people.
No new workflow is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether any course attendance duration is prescribed
research_questions: Does observed training contain redundant administration distinct from learning time?

already_counted.description: All training attendance, practice, and clarification

incremental.description: No added platform or capture duty

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; gross 0%, incremental 0%, net 0%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review building plans and blueprints for fire safety code compliance.

steps.what: Review blueprints and plans against applicable fire safety codes and building use
Resolve fire safety interpretations and document the plan review conclusion

tasks.design: Use existing {DOCS} drawing viewers and review checklists while retaining human code interpretation. The inspector resolves missing information and records a reasoned conclusion for the building reviewer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fire safety depends on the interaction of use, geometry, construction details, and applicable provisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native drawing annotation helps review but no verified structured building model or rule set is supplied here.
tasks.still_hard: Alternative solutions and incomplete drawings require professional interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector recognises when apparently compliant details fail in the building context.
tasks.altitude: Own the fire safety interpretation rather than treating drawing checks as compliance decisions.

reach.learn: Which plan details affect emergency access in practice

evidence.claim: A drawing viewer does not by itself establish fire code compliance or remove interpretive review.

assumptions: This is plan review, not site inspection or issuing an enforcement decision.
No structured dimensions, occupancy code, or compliance flag is assumed to exist for a machine; the inspector reads and interprets source plans within s1.
Native viewers and checklists are retained; a bespoke rule engine is not justified without verified model inputs and recurring check coverage.
No new system or extra capture requirement is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether submissions contain reliable machine readable building models
How many code checks are stable and numerically defined
research_questions: Across ten actual submissions, which checks have complete authoritative inputs and unambiguous rules?

already_counted.description: Reading drawings, locating provisions, and identifying missing information

incremental.description: No proposed automation or added data preparation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+35=100. No removed review work or incremental overhead: net 0%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach fire investigation techniques to firefighting personnel.

steps.what: Teach fire investigation techniques through demonstrations, discussion, and corrective feedback

tasks.design: Retain live instruction and feedback with the investigator, using existing {DOCS} examples. The task does not establish a separate repeated materials production workload to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching techniques requires observing learner reasoning and correcting practical mistakes.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable digital examples can support instruction but do not replace instructor attention.
tasks.still_hard: Learners can reproduce a sequence without understanding evidence contamination or uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor adapts demonstrations and feedback to each learner's misconceptions.
tasks.altitude: Develop sound investigative reasoning in personnel.

reach.learn: Which investigation mistakes compromise later interpretation

evidence.claim: Live technical instruction includes observation and corrective feedback that a material generator does not remove.

assumptions: The boundary is teaching techniques, excluding a separately commissioned course development project.
Native document examples remain in use; no assistant or bespoke learning platform is proposed.
No machine consumes an assumed competence score; the instructor observes learning during counted teaching time.
No new process is deployed, leaving zero incremental software upkeep.
unknowns: How much instruction is practical versus discussion
Whether materials preparation is separately allocated
research_questions: Does a time observation identify repeated material assembly outside live teaching?

already_counted.description: Demonstration, learner observation, and corrective feedback

incremental.description: No added system or data capture work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0%, no incremental workload.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct evacuation drills and evaluate fire exit procedures.

steps.what: Conduct fire exit drills and monitor evacuation behaviour on site
Evaluate evacuation procedures and discuss observed drill weaknesses

tasks.design: Keep on-site drill conduct and evaluation with the inspector; {OTHER} denotes existing drill timing equipment. Use {DOCS} for procedure references and discuss corrective actions with the building safety coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: An evacuation drill tests real behaviour and physical escape routes.
tasks.enabler_now: Timing equipment already assists observation without establishing that people evacuated safely or followed procedures.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour, accessibility, blocked routes, and drill realism need contextual evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: The inspector notices unsafe behaviour and explains practical corrections.
tasks.altitude: Use drills to expose weaknesses in actual evacuation practice.

reach.learn: Which obstacles recur during normal building use

evidence.claim: Timing a drill does not replace observation or evaluation of evacuation behaviour.

assumptions: This boundary covers conducting and evaluating drills, without an invented scheduling or report production segment.
OTHER means existing timing equipment; its present automation receives no new savings credit.
No automatic pass flag or assumed occupant tracking data is introduced; observations remain counted in s1.
No new platform is deployed, so incremental capture and upkeep are zero.
research_questions: Would an observed drill reveal repeated administration distinct from on-site evaluation?

incremental.description: No added software or monitoring process

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Maintain accountable fire safety interpretation, field observation, and technical teaching.
reach: Discuss evidence handling with police identification personnel
role.ambitious_version: An inspector who develops stronger practical judgement and identifies specific repeatable checks before seeking automation.
